correctness.rationale: PASS: Classical Hardy averaging bounds Cα, finite-difference L has dense image and Cα L=I on finite support. B=Cα*L is bounded by Copson and shift bounds; BCα=Cα*, so Qα=Cα*(I−B*B)Cα. The phase-normalized Gram matrix is HS and has the stated rank-one/ordered-area quadratic form. Real shifts yield zero/one negative direction; four disjoint harmonic blocks with phases 1,iσ,−1,−iσ yield arbitrarily many orthogonal strictly negative directions when v≠0. Hilbert–Schmidt perturbation estimate is summable. Finite Gram and phase tests corroborate only the algebra.
